passages.text: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples. And after encouraging them, he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.
passages.sermon:
The uproar ended.
Paul sent for the disciples.
Paul encouraged the disciples.
Paul said goodbye to them.
Paul left to go to Macedonia.
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ παύσασθαι τὸν θόρυβον μεταπεμψάμενος ὁ Παῦλος τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ παρακαλέσας ἀσπασάμενος ἐξῆλθεν πορεύεσθαι εἰς Μακεδονίαν

passages.text: After traveling through that area and speaking many words of encouragement, he arrived in Greece, where he stayed three months. And when the Jews formed a plot against him as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian leader and missionary.
Paul traveled through that area.
He spoke many words of encouragement to the people there.
He arrived in Greece.
He stayed in Greece for three months.
The Jews formed a plot against Paul.
This happened as Paul was about to sail for Syria.
Paul decided not to sail for Syria.
He chose to return by going back through Macedonia.
passages.original: διελθὼν δὲ τὰ μέρη ἐκεῖνα καὶ παρακαλέσας αὐτοὺς λόγῳ πολλῷ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα ποιήσας τε μῆνας τρεῖς γενομένης ἐπιβουλῆς αὐτῷ ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων μέλλοντι ἀνάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν Συρίαν ἐγένετο γνώμης τοῦ ὑποστρέφειν διὰ Μακεδονίας

passages.text: Paul was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.
passages.sermon:
Paul traveled with several men.
Sopater came from Berea.
Sopater was the son of Pyrrhus.
Aristarchus came from Thessalonica.
Secundus also came from Thessalonica.
Gaius came from Derbe.
Timothy traveled with them.
Tychicus came from the province of Asia.
Trophimus also came from the province of Asia.
passages.original: Συνείπετο δὲ αὐτῷ Σώπατρος Πύρρου Βεροιαῖος Θεσσαλονικέων δὲ Ἀρίσταρχος καὶ Σεκοῦνδος καὶ Γάϊος Δερβαῖος καὶ Τιμόθεος Ἀσιανοὶ δὲ Τυχικὸς καὶ Τρόφιμος

passages.text: These men went on ahead and waited for us in Troas.
passages.sermon: These men went on ahead.\r\nThey waited for us in Troas.
passages.original: οὗτοι δὲ προελθόντες ἔμενον ἡμᾶς ἐν Τρῳάδι

passages.text: And after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi, and five days later we rejoined them in Troas, where we stayed seven days.
passages.sermon:
We are Paul and his companions.
We left Philippi after the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
We sailed from Philippi.
After five days, we arrived in Troas.
We met our companions in Troas.
We stayed in Troas for seven days.
passages.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐξεπλεύσαμεν μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας τῶν ἀζύμων ἀπὸ Φιλίππων καὶ ἤλθομεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Τρῳάδα ἄχρι ἡμερῶν πέντε ὅπου διετρίψαμεν ἡμέρας ἑπτά

passages.text: On the first day of the week we came together to break bread. Since Paul was ready to leave the next day, he talked to them and kept on speaking until midnight.
passages.sermon:
We were followers of Jesus.
We gathered on the first day of the week.
We came together to break bread.
Paul was with us.
Paul planned to leave the next day.
Paul spoke to us.
Paul kept speaking until midnight.
passages.original: Ἐν δὲ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων συνηγμένων ἡμῶν κλάσαι ἄρτον ὁ Παῦλος διελέγετο αὐτοῖς μέλλων ἐξιέναι τῇ ἐπαύριον παρέτεινέν τε τὸν λόγον μέχρι μεσονυκτίου

passages.text: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.
passages.sermon: We were gathered in the upper room.\r\nMany lamps were in the upper room.
passages.original: Ἦσαν δὲ λαμπάδες ἱκαναὶ ἐν τῷ ὑπερῴῳ οὗ ἦμεν συνηγμένοι

passages.text: And a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third story and was picked up dead.
passages.sermon:
A young man named Eutychus sat in the window.
Paul spoke for a long time.
Eutychus began to fall into a deep sleep.
He became completely overcome by sleep.
Eutychus fell from the third story window.
People picked him up dead.
passages.original: καθεζόμενος δέ τις νεανίας ὀνόματι Εὔτυχος ἐπὶ τῆς θυρίδος καταφερόμενος ὕπνῳ βαθεῖ διαλεγομένου τοῦ Παύλου ἐπὶ πλεῖον κατενεχθεὶς ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἔπεσεν ἀπὸ τοῦ τριστέγου κάτω καὶ ἤρθη νεκρός

passages.text: But Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and embraced him. “Do not be alarmed!” he said. “He is still alive!”
passages.sermon:
Paul was present in the upper room.
A young man named Eutychus fell from the window.
Eutychus was picked up dead.
Paul went down to Eutychus.
Paul threw himself on Eutychus.
Paul embraced Eutychus.
Paul spoke to the people.
Paul said, “Do not be alarmed.”
Paul said, “He is still alive.”
passages.original: καταβὰς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἐπέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ συμπεριλαβὼν εἶπεν Μὴ θορυβεῖσθε ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐστιν

passages.text: Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. And after speaking until daybreak, he departed.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian apostle.
Paul went back upstairs.
Paul broke bread.
Paul ate.
Paul spoke for a long time.
Paul spoke until daybreak.
Paul left.
passages.original: Ἀναβὰς δὲ καὶ κλάσας τὸν ἄρτον καὶ γευσάμενος ἐφ’ ἱκανόν τε ὁμιλήσας ἄχρι αὐγῆς οὕτως ἐξῆλθεν

passages.text: And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive.
passages.sermon: The people took the boy home alive.\r\nThey felt great relief.
passages.original: ἤγαγον δὲ τὸν παῖδα ζῶντα καὶ παρεκλήθησαν οὐ μετρίως

passages.text: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we were to take Paul aboard. He had arranged this because he was going there on foot.
passages.sermon:
We were Paul's companions.
We went ahead of Paul.
We boarded the ship.
We sailed to Assos.
We planned to take Paul aboard at Assos.
Paul had arranged this plan.
Paul was going to Assos on foot.
passages.original: Ἡμεῖς δὲ προελθόντες ἐπὶ τὸ πλοῖον ἀνήχθημεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἆσσον ἐκεῖθεν μέλλοντες ἀναλαμβάνειν τὸν Παῦλον οὕτως γὰρ διατεταγμένος ἦν μέλλων αὐτὸς πεζεύειν

passages.text: And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle and a leader in the early church.
He traveled to many places to spread the message of Jesus.
Paul met us at Assos.
We took Paul aboard the ship.
We went to Mitylene.
passages.original: ὡς δὲ συνέβαλλεν ἡμῖν εἰς τὴν Ἆσσον ἀναλαβόντες αὐτὸν ἤλθομεν εἰς Μιτυλήνην

passages.text: Sailing on from there, we arrived the next day opposite Chios. The day after that we arrived at Samos, and on the following day we came to Miletus.
passages.sermon:
We sailed from Assos.
The next day we reached a place opposite Chios.
The following day we arrived at Samos.
On the day after that we came to Miletus.
passages.original: κἀκεῖθεν ἀποπλεύσαντες τῇ ἐπιούσῃ κατηντήσαμεν ἄντικρυς Χίου τῇ δὲ ἑτέρᾳ παρεβάλομεν εἰς Σάμον τῇ δὲ ἐχομένῃ ἤλθομεν εἰς Μίλητον

passages.text: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus to avoid spending time in the province of Asia, because he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul made a decision.
He decided to sail past Ephesus.
He wanted to avoid spending time in the province of Asia.
Paul was in a hurry.
He wanted to reach Jerusalem as soon as possible.
He hoped to be in Jerusalem by the day of Pentecost.
passages.original: Κεκρίκει γὰρ ὁ Παῦλος παραπλεῦσαι τὴν Ἔφεσον ὅπως μὴ γένηται αὐτῷ χρονοτριβῆσαι ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ ἔσπευδεν γὰρ εἰ δυνατὸν εἴη αὐτῷ τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς γενέσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα

passages.text: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.
passages.sermon: Paul was in Miletus.\r\nPaul sent a message to Ephesus.\r\nHe called for the elders of the church in Ephesus.
passages.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς Μιλήτου πέμψας εἰς Ἔφεσον μετεκαλέσατο τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τῆς ἐκκλησίας

passages.text: When they came to him, he said, “You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I arrived in the province of Asia.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul called the elders of the church in Ephesus to meet him.
The elders came to Paul.
Paul spoke to the elders.
Paul said, "You know how I lived among you."
Paul said, "You know this from the first day I arrived in Asia."
Paul said, "You know how I lived with you the whole time."
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ παρεγένοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ἀπὸ πρώτης ἡμέρας ἀφ’ ἧς ἐπέβην εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν πῶς μεθ’ ὑμῶν τὸν πάντα χρόνον ἐγενόμην

passages.text: I served the Lord with great humility and with tears, especially in the trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.
passages.sermon:
Paul served the Lord.
He served with great humility.
He often wept.
He faced many trials.
These trials came to him because of the plots of the Jews.
passages.original: δουλεύων τῷ Κυρίῳ μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης καὶ δακρύων καὶ πειρασμῶν τῶν συμβάντων μοι ἐν ταῖς ἐπιβουλαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house, testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the elders from Ephesus.
Paul always spoke openly to them.
Paul never held back anything that would help them.
Paul declared everything that was useful for them to know.
Paul taught them in public places.
Paul also taught them in their homes.
Paul testified to both Jews and Greeks.
Paul told everyone to repent and turn to God.
Paul called everyone to have faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: ὡς οὐδὲν ὑπεστειλάμην τῶν συμφερόντων τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι ὑμῖν καὶ διδάξαι ὑμᾶς δημοσίᾳ καὶ κατ’ οἴκους διαμαρτυρόμενος Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν τὴν εἰς Θεὸν μετάνοιαν καὶ πίστιν εἰς τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν

passages.text: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking.
Paul is a servant of the Lord Jesus.
The Holy Spirit compels Paul.
Now Paul is going to Jerusalem.
Paul does not know what will happen to him in Jerusalem.
passages.original: Καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ δεδεμένος ἐγὼ τῷ πνεύματι πορεύομαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ συναντήσοντά μοι μὴ εἰδώς

passages.text: I only know that in town after town the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit speaks to me.
The Holy Spirit warns me in every town.
The Holy Spirit says that chains wait for me.
The Holy Spirit says that afflictions wait for me.
passages.original: πλὴν ὅτι τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον κατὰ πόλιν διαμαρτύρεταί μοι λέγον ὅτι δεσμὰ καὶ θλίψεις με μένουσιν

passages.text: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus—the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a servant of the Lord Jesus.
Paul does not consider his own life valuable to himself.
Paul wants to finish his course.
Paul wants to complete the ministry he received from the Lord Jesus.
Paul’s ministry is to testify to the good news of God’s grace.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ οὐδενὸς λόγου ποιοῦμαι τὴν ψυχὴν τιμίαν ἐμαυτῷ ὡς τελειῶσαι τὸν δρόμον μου καὶ τὴν διακονίαν ἣν ἔλαβον παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ διαμαρτύρασθαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom will see my face again.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the elders in Ephesus.
Paul has preached the kingdom of God among them.
Paul knows something important now.
Paul knows that none of them will see his face again.
Paul says this to all the people among whom he has traveled and preached.
passages.original: Καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ οἶδα ὅτι οὐκέτι ὄψεσθε τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ὑμεῖς πάντες ἐν οἷς διῆλθον κηρύσσων τὴν βασιλείαν

passages.text: Therefore I testify to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all men.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the elders of the church at Ephesus.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul says, “I testify to you today.”
Paul says, “I am innocent of the blood of all people.”
passages.original: διότι μαρτύρομαι ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σήμερον ἡμέρᾳ ὅτι καθαρός εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος πάντων

passages.text: For I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the elders of the church in Ephesus.
Paul is a servant of God.
Paul did not hold back anything.
Paul declared the whole will of God to them.
Paul told them everything God wanted them to know.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ὑπεστειλάμην τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι πᾶσαν τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ὑμῖν

passages.text: Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit has made you overseers.
You are responsible for the church of God.
God purchased this church with His own blood.
Watch over yourselves.
Watch over the entire flock.
Be shepherds to God’s church.
passages.original: Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς καὶ παντὶ τῷ ποιμνίῳ ἐν ᾧ ὑμᾶς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἔθετο ἐπισκόπους ποιμαίνειν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἣν περιεποιήσατο διὰ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ ἰδίου

passages.text: I know that after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the elders of the church in Ephesus.
Paul knows what will happen after he leaves.
After Paul departs, savage wolves will come in among the believers.
These wolves will not spare the flock.
The flock means the church, the people of God.
passages.original: ἐγὼ οἶδα ὅτι εἰσελεύσονται μετὰ τὴν ἄφιξίν μου λύκοι βαρεῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς μὴ φειδόμενοι τοῦ ποιμνίου

passages.text: Even from your own number, men will rise up and distort the truth to draw away disciples after them.
passages.sermon:
Some men will rise up from among you.
These men will come from your own group.
They will speak things that are twisted and false.
They will distort the truth.
They will try to lead disciples away from the truth.
They want the disciples to follow them instead.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν ἀναστήσονται ἄνδρες λαλοῦντες διεστραμμένα τοῦ ἀποσπᾶν τοὺς μαθητὰς ὀπίσω ἑαυτῶν

passages.text: Therefore be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the elders of the church in Ephesus.
Paul urges them to stay alert.
Paul tells them to remember his example.
For three years, Paul warned each of them.
He did this every night and every day.
He never stopped warning them.
He warned them with tears.
passages.original: διὸ γρηγορεῖτε μνημονεύοντες ὅτι τριετίαν νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν οὐκ ἐπαυσάμην μετὰ δακρύων νουθετῶν ἕνα ἕκαστον

passages.text: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the elders of the church at Ephesus.
Paul said, “Now I commit you to God.
I also commit you to the word of God’s grace.
God’s grace can build you up.
God’s grace can give you an inheritance.
This inheritance belongs to all who are sanctified.”
passages.original: Καὶ τὰ νῦν παρατίθεμαι ὑμᾶς τῷ θεῷ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ τῷ δυναμένῳ οἰκοδομῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν κληρονομίαν ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πᾶσιν

passages.text: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the elders of the church at Ephesus.
Paul says he did not desire anyone’s silver.
He did not desire anyone’s gold.
He did not desire anyone’s clothing.
passages.original: Ἀργυρίου ἢ χρυσίου ἢ ἱματισμοῦ οὐδενὸς ἐπεθύμησα

passages.text: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the elders in Ephesus.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul says, “You know this.”
Paul says, “These hands of mine have worked.”
Paul says, “My hands have provided for my own needs.”
Paul says, “My hands have also provided for the needs of my companions.”
passages.original: αὐτοὶ γινώσκετε ὅτι ταῖς χρείαις μου καὶ τοῖς οὖσιν μετ’ ἐμοῦ ὑπηρέτησαν αἱ χεῖρες αὗται

passages.text: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the elders of the church at Ephesus.
Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Paul showed the elders how to live by his own example.
Paul worked hard in every way.
Paul taught that we must help people who are weak.
Paul told them to remember the words of the Lord Jesus.
Jesus said, “It is more blessed to give than to receive.”
passages.original: πάντα ὑπέδειξα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως κοπιῶντας δεῖ ἀντιλαμβάνεσθαι τῶν ἀσθενούντων μνημονεύειν τε τῶν λόγων τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ ὅτι αὐτὸς εἶπεν Μακάριόν ἐστιν μᾶλλον διδόναι ἢ λαμβάνειν

passages.text: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the people.
Paul finished speaking.
Paul knelt down.
All the people knelt down with Paul.
Paul prayed with them.
passages.original: Καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν θεὶς τὰ γόνατα αὐτοῦ σὺν πᾶσιν αὐτοῖς προσηύξατο

passages.text: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.
passages.sermon: All the people wept openly.\r\nThey embraced Paul.\r\nThey kissed him.
passages.original: ἱκανὸς δὲ κλαυθμὸς ἐγένετο πάντων καὶ ἐπιπεσόντες ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τοῦ Παύλου κατεφίλουν αὐτόν

passages.text: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian leader.
He told the people they would never see his face again.
His words caused them great sorrow.
They felt deep grief.
They walked with Paul to the ship.
passages.original: ὀδυνώμενοι μάλιστα ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ᾧ εἰρήκει ὅτι οὐκέτι μέλλουσιν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ θεωρεῖν προέπεμπον δὲ αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον
